items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: as Malcolm X said one time, he said, “the most segregated time in America is 12 o’clock on Sundays”

ctx.x: Did you notice a positive or negative circumstances that followed that merging of the union?

I saw both actually. I mean in the long run it was good because segregation in any form, you know based on race, gender, religion, is always — I mean even as a kid I was raised in the African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church and I used to wonder why — I mean it was segregated you know what I mean? If you — if a white person came to serve, to worship and sat down, people would be wondering oh, who is that? What’s he doing here? You know. I mean this was in the ‘50s you know, up north in Buffalo. And so we had this…
building. And the reason they didn’t lose the building is because it was incorporated away from the union. It has its own incorporation status.
